valuation_philosophy: Nu Holdings is a deposit-funded digital bank; conventional FCF (OCF minus capex) is meaningless because operating cash flow is dominated by deposit inflows and loan-book growth, not owner earnings. This model values NU's EQUITY directly using a residual-income / distributable-earnings approach: distributable_t = NetIncome_t x (1 - retention_t), where retention_t = growth_t / ROE_t is the fraction of earnings that must be reinvested to fund balance-sheet growth at a steady equity/assets ratio (NU's equity/assets was ~16.25% at Q1 2026: 12,588.8/77,456.4). In early projection years NU's growth (35%+) exceeds its ROE (~28%), implying retention >100% (floored at 100%) -- i.e., near-zero distributable earnings -- which matches reality: NU pays no dividend and only just announced its first-ever buyback ($1bn, June 2026) because it is still retaining essentially all capital to fund hypergrowth. The terminal value uses a SEPARATE, internally consistent retention ratio (terminal_growth / terminal_ROE, using a mature/normalized ROE distinct from the Y5 growth-year ROE) rather than carrying forward the Y5 high-growth retention rate -- using the Y5 retention rate directly would double-count reinvestment (it assumes earnings keep compounding at ~15-22% forever while only being discounted at a much lower terminal growth rate, which inflates value). The result is a standard Gordon-growth DDM: implied terminal P/E = payout_ratio / (CoE - terminal_growth), cross-checked against (and capped by) an explicit exit P/E on Year-5 net income. All cash flows are discounted at COST OF EQUITY (labeled 'wacc' in the JSON schema for compatibility with the dashboard, but it is cost of equity, not a blended WACC with debt -- appropriate because deposits/borrowings are operating liabilities of a bank, not financing debt). net_debt is set to 0: cash, deposits and borrowings are operating balance-sheet items for a bank, not a financing net-debt position to net against enterprise value.

historical_growth.fcf_note: Not applicable/meaningful - NU is a deposit-funded bank; operating cash flow is dominated by deposit inflows and loan growth, not owner FCF. Distributable earnings used instead (see valuation_philosophy).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: net_income_growth_path (decelerating: 35% -> 28% -> 22% -> 18% -> 15%), not a single historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue 3yr CAGR (48.8%), equity 3yr CAGR (32.2%) and net income 2yr CAGR (66.9%) all reflect NU's hypergrowth 2022-2025 era and diverge sharply from each other and from any sustainable long-run rate. All historical CAGRs are decelerated aggressively in the projection (base case starts at 35% net income growth in Y1, well below trailing rates, and falls to 15% by Y5, then further to 3.75% terminal growth) per analyst consensus of ~30% near-term EPS growth fading over time.

base.implied_exit_multiple_note: Implied exit P/E on Year-5 net income; current TTM P/E is ~21.7x, so this base case implies significant multiple contraction, not expansion (conservative).

entry_price.methodology: Entry = (sum of scenario distributable earnings Y1-Y5 discounted at 15% + terminal value (computed at CoE, per scenario) discounted at 15% - net_debt) / shares. Uses each scenario's own decelerating flow path and terminal value, not a terminal-only shortcut.

sensitivity.note: Base case scenario structure (growth path, ROE path, exit P/E cap) with CoE and terminal growth varied

historical_averages_ex_outliers.ev_ebitda_note: EV/EBITDA not meaningful for a deposit-funded bank

sanity_check.diagnosis: No over-valuation detected. Base-case IV $9.52 implies 16.3x trailing P/E and 4.1x P/B, both well below NU's own history (avg P/E ~31x, max P/B 7.3x). The model is conservative by construction: all scenarios assume multiple contraction (implied exit P/E 7-10x vs current 21.7x), terminal retention is recomputed at mature-bank ROE, and discounting uses a 13.5% cost of equity for LatAm/credit-cycle risk. Note the check guards against over-valuation only; the market currently prices NU well above the model's probability-weighted IV of $9.56.
